major: Scene 3 'Change one fact', sentences 1-2: the padlocked gate is drawn between Mara and the running dog (Mara at the wall, gate, then dog approaching from the right). Read as staged, the locked gate is a barrier protecting her, contradicting the source example (B.1: the gate is her blocked escape, high threat/low control -> fear). In sentence 2 the padlock simply vanishes while the gate stays drawn closed and the dog keeps advancing, so 'Now she can shut the gate' is not visible (the gate already looks shut) and the change reads as the barrier being unlocked/threat increasing rather than Mara gaining control. Only the small device in her hand carries the intended meaning. Restage so the dog is on Mara's side of an open/escape gate (or the gate is her blocked exit behind/beside her), and show the gate as open-but-closable via her device in the variant.
minor: Night theme swaps the man's and Mara's dark navy trousers (and chair legs) to pale grey; faces, hair and coats keep identity, but clothing is not stable across themes.
Scene 2 radar 'appraisal vector' uses unlabelled illustrative values; acceptable as a schematic but the right half of the stage stays empty through sentence 2.
Scene 3 paired radars: 'Fear' label is red while 'Anger' is ink-coloured; inconsistent label treatment.
Scene 1 'Agent <-> world' connector endpoint grazes the speech-bubble corner/window edge.
At 320 px the 'AI judge' label becomes very small.

checkedOk: Scene 1: seated man has a visibly sad face against the rain window while saying 'I'm perfectly fine'; magnifier highlights 'fine' and the AI judge shows 'Calm', then 'Calm' is struck through as the agent-world relationship line appears. Magnifier never crosses a face.
Scene 2: episode/mood/sentiment/attitude bars on a seconds->years axis, six labelled appraisal axes, fear/anger prototype blobs with separate confidence and intensity bars match their sentences.

Scene 3: Mara shows a distinct fear face in sentence 1 and anger brows/mouth in sentence 2; owner with dropped leash shows the deliberate release; minimal-pair radars and closing Chapter 1 book match the narration.
No caption collisions, ghosts, duplicated limbs or props over faces observed; titles single and readable; Color/Light/Dark keep backgrounds flat; fades at 15% are authored reveals.
